B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No MCP-specific fee is stated in the reviewed official material. Contact unlock uses the user's existing Sales Intelligence credits; the docs do not state charges for other documented retrieval capabilities.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Revenue Marketing access is required for marketing capabilities; Sales Intelligence access is required for supported sales capabilities. Official pricing pages reviewed do not publish amounts.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Contact unlock consumes existing Sales Intelligence credits. 6sense says credit allocations depend on the purchased product package and sales contract. No MCP per-call price or general MCP quota was found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Each user must individually authorize access. Capabilities depend on the user's 6sense license, role, and organization AI/MCP settings. The organization-level AI and MCP feature control is off by default. AI-platform administrators may restrict connector availability.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: 6sense organization administrators control AI/MCP feature access; 6sense controls licenses, roles, and account permissions; AI-platform administrators may restrict connector installation; each end user authorizes their own connection.

The endpoint returned HTTP 401 and a WWW-Authenticate challenge referencing https://api.6sense.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp. The authorization metadata does not publish token lifetime. The endpoint-origin protected-resource URL without the /mcp suffix returned 404.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official documentation states all MCP operations are read-only. No official tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are published; no tool schemas are available to inspect. 2. No server-enforced confirmation mechanism is documented. Contact unlock consumes existing Sales Intelligence credits, but the documentation does not describe a confirmation step. 3. OAuth scopes are mcp:use and offline_access. Access honors the user's 6sense license and role; each user separately authorizes. Organization AI/MCP feature control is off by default and can be toggled by admins. OAuth metadata supports DCR, PKCE S256, and publishes a revocation endpoint; token lifetime is not published. 4. No documented read-only mode switch, toolset filter, URL/header selector, or sandbox endpoint. The only documented product behavior is read-only. One global endpoint is provided. 5. Docs say contact-level website activity is limited to known CRM records and does not de-anonymize anonymous visitors. Each connector is isolated to its separately authorized 6sense instance. 6. Contact unlock uses existing Sales Intelligence credits. No MCP-specific rate limits, result caps, time-range caps, or truncation behavior found. 7. No parameter validation, coercion, aliasing, or operator-argument override behavior documented; no public code found. 8. MCP-specific audit logging and telemetry are not documented. The privacy policy describes general personal-information processing and retention, but not MCP request logs. 9. No vendor feedback/rating/survey tool or MCP-specific upsell result found in available descriptions. Contact unlock is credit-consuming. 10. The server uses Revvy AI subagents per official FAQ. No server-delivered skills or initialize instructions are documented. 11. No evidence that prior agent behavior changes later outputs or available MCP tools. Docs note responses may vary with phrasing and AI outputs are nondeterministic. 12. Official docs describe an integration layer using Revvy AI subagents; no separate MCP sub-server hierarchy or alternate official endpoint was found. The subagent-backed retrieval is a nested vendor AI capability. 13. No raw API request, SQL, script execution, or equivalent escape hatch is documented in the available tool descriptions; actual authenticated tool list unavailable.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool list is not published by name: the official support article describes 10 functional scenario categories but no machine tool names, stated total, or schemas. Agent Discoverability (2026-10) names 3 actions; these are included as third-party additions, with parameters marked NOT PUBLISHED where absent. Other catalogues describe capabilities but provide no exact tool names: StackMCP lists 10 capability areas; Work Insiders and MartechDB say names are only available after sign-in; APIs.io has no tool list for this server. Claude directory returned HTTP 403 and Claude.com/connectors returned 404. The three catalogue names have not been verified against the authenticated endpoint.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The FAQ says the AI assistant automatically selects tools based on the query. Official docs also guide users toward read-only retrieval, but do not publish authenticated tool instructions or enforcement details. Verbatim: “The AI assistant selects tools automatically based on the query.”
F_documentation.governance_promises: 6sense states that access follows the user's license and role, each user authorizes individually, and connectors remain isolated by the 6sense instance authorized. Contact-level website activity is limited to known CRM records and does not de-anonymize anonymous visitors. The FAQ says handling, storage, and retention after transfer are determined by the AI assistant platform. Verbatim: “Data is not shared between connectors.”
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The current release is described as read-only; MCP retrieves selected account data and insights through Revvy-powered scenarios. The vendor says users can connect multiple 6sense instances using separate connector authorizations.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Read-only status and organization AI/MCP controls are documented, but no public code or authenticated tool metadata was available to independently verify them. The instance-scoping and known-contact restrictions are documented product behaviors, with enforcement implementation not exposed. Post-transfer data handling is explicitly assigned to the connected AI platform. The privacy policy contains general retention language but does not specify MCP-specific retention or training handling.

contradictions: Official support documentation describes 10 functional capability areas without tool names; Agent Discoverability lists 3 exact tool names. These are different levels of description and cannot be reconciled to an authenticated tool inventory from the available evidence.
observations_for_research: Access is controlled at several layers: user OAuth authorization, 6sense license and role, organization-level AI/MCP feature settings, and potentially AI-platform connector policy.
The endpoint uses a global URL while documentation supports multiple isolated 6sense instances through separate connector authorizations; instance choice is left to the user and AI platform.
Contact unlock is a read-only MCP capability that consumes an existing product credit allocation, so read-only does not imply cost-free.
